summary: A 1952 two-story L-4 lookout on Crater Lake's highest summit, no longer staffed and now used for USGS seismic equipment and emergencies.

facts.design: Two-story modified L-4, about 14 x 14 ft, with a fold-up catwalk
facts.agency: U.S. Dept. of the Interior; National Park Service is the cooperator (Crater Lake National Park)

access.note: Maintained for emergency use; houses USGS seismic monitoring equipment. The sources read do not say whether visitors may go inside the cab.

visit.trail_note: About 2.5 miles with many switchbacks, starting on Rim Drive and ending at the tower on the summit. Trailhead at 7,683 ft (Wikipedia).

events.note: First structure, a cupola cabin. Register gives 1924; firelookout.com says about 1923; a history page places a three-way agreement in winter 1924/25
In August 1928 the lookout reported seven fires on the reservation, one on the Crater National Forest and two on Association territory
Materials delivered to build the lookout house; a lookout offered to build it and did much of the work by the end of the fire season
Still a cooperative lookout between Crater Lake National Park and the Klamath district of the Rogue River National Forest
Current two-story structure replaced the cupola, which had become too loose to plot fire locations
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, December 1, 2002

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 1924 and firelookout.com gives about 1923 for the first cupola cabin. A history page places a three-way agreement in winter 1924/25 and says the lookout house materials arrived in 1929. The story reports the disagreement and does not pick one year.

The register and cherylhill blog describe a cupola cabin built in the 1920s. The history page says the lookout house was being built in 1929. These can be read as the same building, dated differently.

sources.title: Mt. Scott, Every Lookout in Oregon

notes_for_editor: Current status is consistent across the register (emergency use), firelookout.com (available for emergencies) and the 2024 blog (not staffed, USGS equipment). The founding date is disputed (1923, 1924, or 1924/25 with the house built 1929). Elevation differs: NHLR 8,806 ft; firelookout.com 8926 ft; Wikipedia 8,934 ft (not used in the story). The NHLR 1977 visit report lists staffing as Sometimes; not used because it is dated. The brief's agency 'U.S. Dept. of the Interior' matches the register; the NPS is named as cooperator. Willhite Web is a personal history site that reproduces park files; treat its dates as secondary. Not read: any Crater Lake NPS page on visitor access to the cab.
